observables.expectation_basis: This workspace has already delivered -0.4727 V for the same couple at PBE0-D3BJ/def2-SVP + CPCM(MeCN) from Gibbs free energies of the validated neutral and doublet-cation minima; a thiolate-rich Ni(II)/Ni(III) pair with two alkyl phosphines sits well below Fc+/Fc.
observables.meaning: The one-electron +1/0 oxidation potential of the PMe3 model complex [Ni(SMe)2(PMe3)2]+/0 in acetonitrile, on the ferrocenium/ferrocene scale, as a best estimate from the registered and newly computed evidence.
observables.tolerance_basis: Task words: 'a potential versus ferrocene in acetonitrile good to about plus or minus 0.2 V, which is enough to choose among those three oxidants'.

observables.expectation_basis: A d7 Ni(III) centre in a square-planar S2P2 field puts most of the single hole in a metal-centred orbital, with delocalisation onto the two thiolates; this workspace has already delivered 0.809 (Mulliken) and 0.787 (Loewdin) for the same result.
observables.meaning: Mulliken spin population on the nickel atom of the relaxed doublet cation of the PMe3 model complex, i.e. how much of the unpaired electron the metal carries.

observables.expectation_basis: Thiolate S 3p orbitals mix strongly with the Ni d manifold, so each sulfur carries a fraction of the hole; the same result previously gave 0.118.
observables.meaning: Mulliken spin population on the first thiolate sulfur of the relaxed doublet cation of the PMe3 model complex.

observables.expectation_basis: The two thiolates are symmetry-equivalent in the trans square-planar arrangement, so the second sulfur should match the first to within relaxation asymmetry; the same result previously gave 0.118.
observables.meaning: Mulliken spin population on the second thiolate sulfur of the relaxed doublet cation of the PMe3 model complex.

observables.expectation_basis: This workspace delivered 0.2191 eV from the two validated def2-SVP/CPCM minima; a strong-field S2P2 donor set should keep the low-spin doublet below the quartet, but the quartet is not far enough away to dismiss without computing it.
observables.meaning: Gibbs free energy of the relaxed quartet cation minus that of the relaxed doublet cation of the PMe3 model complex at 298.15 K, i.e. whether the quartet is competitive with the doublet.

observables.expectation_basis: Both partners are the same molecule differing by one electron on a metal-dominated orbital; the def2-SVP to def2-TZVP differential on such a difference is usually a few tens of meV, and the prior goal named exactly this as the unmeasured component of its 0.25 V asserted uncertainty.
observables.failure_update_rule: If |basis shift| exceeds 0.05 V, the SVP Gibbs couple is not defensible as the delivered value: the basis-corrected couple becomes the delivery and the measured shift is carried as an evidence-backed uncertainty component rather than an asserted one.
observables.meaning: The shift in the +1/0 couple, in volts, produced by re-evaluating both redox partners at def2-TZVP instead of def2-SVP on their own def2-SVP geometries.

failure_report.diagnosis: the previous cycle ended 'complete' (no workflow was planned; the session ended: host readiness gates passed) having delivered every declared observable, with these requirements unresolved: e-couple-vs-fc-pme3: uncertainty 0.165712 V is within the required 0.2 V and rests on your own word
failure_report.invariant: a requested observable is resolved when its stated uncertainty is within the tolerance the task asked for and rests on evidence the host can resolve, or when the session refuses it with receipts. A number delivered with no uncertainty beside it, or short of what was asked, with budget in hand, is none of those. An uncertainty is a judgement about a result, so a delivery that came from an executed plan carries none until a session looks at what came back.
failure_report.route: back it or bound it: your uncertainty is within the tolerance and rests on your own word, or leaves a term unquantified, so the requirement stands open. Cite the receipt the magnitude comes from and claim again with basis measured or inferred; or measure the term you could not -- a conformer search, one method axis changed -- and cite that; or refuse it with the receipts that show the gap. Citing a receipt you already hold costs no engine call and so does refusing; only measuring a term you have not measured spends one. Naming a term you cannot quantify is the honest act and it is why this is open: saying so is a delivery, and dropping the term to close the word is not.

observables.expectation_basis: The registry documents those two entries as one convention family whose stated purpose is to be combined onto the ferrocene scale, so they should reproduce the direct entry to within a few tens of millivolts; the check is aimed at my own delivery, which subtracts this constant from an absolute ionisation free energy and would inherit any inconsistency volt for volt.

decision_uncertainties: The CPCM-specific systematic on the 0/+1 differential solvation of this pair is NOT in the 0.167348 V and cannot be measured in this workspace: every registered level uses CPCM, so there is no gas-phase or alternative-model counterpart to difference against. Two things bound its impact rather than excuse its absence: the same continuum model and solvent also enter the ferrocene reference couple, so the leading systematic is common-mode to the subtraction; and the whole delivered interval [-0.561497, -0.226801] V lies below the mildest oxidant on the shelf, so a solvation error of order 0.2 V would not change the oxidant choice, which is what the tolerance exists to support. A number for the real compound rather than the model would require buying that pair of calculations.

Transfer from the model to the real compound is unbounded here and is the dominant limitation on answering the experimental question. The workspace's own PH3-versus-PMe3 comparison moved the same couple by 0.196 V, so ligand substitution is a few-tenths-of-a-volt effect; an aryl thiolate is a weaker donor than SMe and should shift the couple positive, while dmpe chelation shifts it the other way. Nothing in this workspace separates those two for 2,6-dimethylbenzenethiolate/dmpe.

The delivered value sits at the edge of its own functional spread, and the spread is one-sided: PBE0 -0.394149, B3LYP -0.523195, TPSSh -0.541109 V. A symmetric error bar is what the budget can express, but the evidence says the couple is at least as negative as the delivered value and probably more negative. This is a finding about the delivery, not a defect in it.

RRHO is weakest exactly where the host flagged it: three sub-50 cm^-1 modes on the neutral (21.07 kJ/mol of T*S) and two on the cation (13.54 kJ/mol). The measured electronic/RRHO/qRRHO spread of 0.012906 V is small because both partners are equally floppy and the term largely cancels in the difference; that is a cancellation, not an absence, and a conformer change on one partner only would not cancel.

uncertainty-e-couple-pme3 is 0.167348 V against the previous cycle's inferred 0.165712 V, a 1.0% difference, because the decomposition changed (functional term put on a consistent RRHO footing, reference-scale term added). The two totals agreeing to 1% is itself evidence that the total is not sensitive to how it is decomposed.

couple-b3-corr-pme3 and couple-tp-corr-pme3 differ from the previous cycle's couple-b3lyp-basiscorr-pme3 (-0.5290) and couple-tpssh-basiscorr-pme3 (-0.5470) by exactly 0.004863 V, the PBE0 RRHO thermal term. New claim ids were used so the record does not carry two values under one name; both footings are defensible and the difference is smaller than any term in the budget.
